title.narrative: Upgrading and Greening the Rio de Janeiro Urban Rail System

description.narrative: (a) to improve the level of service provided to suburban rail transport users in the RJMR in a safe and cost-efficient manner; (b) to place the suburban rail transport system on a lower carbon growth path; and (c) to improve the transport management and policy framework in the Borrower's territory and in the RJMR.

The objectives of the Second Rio de Janeiro Mass Transit Project for Brazil is to: a) improve the level-of-service provided to the suburban rail transport users in Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Region (RJMR) in a safe and cost-efficient manner; and b) to improve the transport management and policy framework in the RJMR. There are two components to the project, the first component being infrastructure and equipment. Acquisition of at least thirty trains Electric Multiple Unit (EMU) of four cars each and accessories for a total of at least 120 cars to be operated, on the lines of state agency in charge of the suburban railway system (CENTRAL), by the concessionaire under the terms of the concessionaire contract. This component represents about 97 percent of the total project cost. Finally, the second component is the institutional and policy development. Provision of technical assistance to Rio de Janeiro State Secretariat for Transport (SETRANS) for the carrying out of studies on policy development, including: (i) consolidating the Metropolitan Urban Transport Authority of Rio de Janeiro (AMTU-RJ) for the RJMR; (ii) updating the current integrated transport policy, land use and air quality management master plan (PDTU) for the RJMR to meet both transport and air quality targets and to introduce sound cost-recovery, tariff, regulatory, and subsidy policies; and (iii) supporting the adoption of integrated modal tariffs. Provision of technical assistance to CENTRAL for the management and supervision of the project, will include the acquisition and reception of the trains (EMU). This component represents about three percent of the total project cost.

title.narrative: Component 1b. Additional demand generated from project on SuperVia -passengers per day

comment.narrative: <p>The target has been adjusted from 70,211 to 0. Demand has been severely affected by a series of exogenous impacts, first the economic crisis in the State of Rio de Janeiro since 2016 followed by COVID-19. This indicator was the highest in 2016, reaching 118,536 and thus meeting the target, but demand has eroded since. In 2020 demand was below the baseline in 2009 and is only expected to bounce back in 2025.</p>

comment.narrative: The indicator was previously a PDO Indicator and was moved to an Intermediate Indicator. It continues to be a relevant indicator to track, however it does not measure a project outcome given that operational speeds have been reduced to ensure safe operations of the newly acquired trains. In addition, travel time is also dependent on integrated systems such as signaling and power supply. No new Project activities are expected to have an impact on this indicator.

The indicator, included in the last restructuring, measures energy efficiency from the new rolling stock acquisition, which would reduce the carbon emission per train-km and place the system on a lower carbon growth path.

This is an annual indicator (average of two semesters) and 2022 will be reported when the second semester ends.
ASK reflects additional capacity added with the new trains. From the first half of 2020, the supply of seats was compromised by the pandemic, following the demand curve. The gradual resumption of the supply of seats was scheduled for Mar/22, however, it was postponed due to the degradation scenario generated by the theft of copper cables.
Pre-pandemic levels were considerably above the baeline and met the target:
2015 - 17,984,784,939
2016 - 19,263,540,712
2017 - 19,611,502,272
2018 - 19,355,016,196
2019 - 19,282,925,692

The acquisition of new trains is expected to significantly increase the satisfaction of the users with the system. This indicator was included as an intermediate indicator due to the lack of a baseline before 2014 - only started to be measured at the same time the new trains were being put in operation.
The user satisfaction survey was interrupted during the Covid-19 pandemicnd has not been resumed in time to supply the associated indicator.
